unresolved: Table 3 per-species Pb means (0.058-0.061) cannot be reconciled with Table 2 overall Pb mean 0.029 mg/kg.

Exceedance counts (As 1, Hg 2, Pb 10 over Chinese MAC; text also says 4 of 248 chicken muscle samples Pb>0.2) and exposure doses/THQ/HI (Table 5) are not findings; no per-species P97.5 or range printed. Figure 2 per-species means are figure-only. Text says mutton had significantly lower As, Cd, Cr (P<0.05), but Table 3 Cd is 0.002 for all and the species Pb/Cd differences are not testable.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: China MAC in meat (GB 2762-2017, as cited)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: As 0.5, Cd 0.1, Cr 1, Hg 0.05, Pb 0.2 mg/kg

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Mean dietary exposure by meat intake 112.9 g/day

source_record_corrections: Primary text is the Research Square preprint (rs-1102078/v1, 30 Nov 2021) although the file is named s41598-022-07214-3.pdf (the Sci Rep 2022 article); preprint text is what was read.

Real title: Distribution and Safety Assessment of Heavy Metals in Fresh Meat from Zhejiang, China. Authors: Jian Long Han, Xiao Dong Pan, Qing Chen. Record title 'Keywords: Meat, Heavy metal...' is a scrape; record matrices (fish, seaweed) and jurisdiction US are wrong: matrix is fresh meat, jurisdiction CN.
Record metals list includes Al which is not measured; Cu measured but not listed.
